abstract: AIM: To study the outcome of cases of incidental adnexal masses detected during cesarean section. METHODS: A total of 126 093 live births and 39 115 cesarean deliveries performed between 2002 and 2008 were retrospectively evaluated and cases with additional adnexal masses and surgical interventions were included in the study. Histopathologic assessment and related outcomes were examined. RESULTS: One hundred and nineteen patients had incidental adnexal masses at the time of cesarean delivery; the incidence of adnexal masses was 1/329. The most common histopathologic diagnoses were mature cystic teratoma (32%) and functional cysts (26%). Six cases (5%) were bilateral. The mean cyst size was 6.4 cm; two of the masses were malignant. CONCLUSION: Incidental masses detected at the time of cesarean section should be extirpated in order to exclude the possibility of malignancy and to avoid additional surgical procedures following cesarean section.
abstract_ja: 目的：帝王切開時に偶発的に発見された付属器腫瘤の経過を検討する。方法：2002年から2008年の間に行われた126,093例の生児出産と39,115例の帝王切開を後方視的に評価し、付属器腫瘤の合併および外科的処置を伴う症例を対象とした。組織病理学的評価と関連する転帰を検討した。結果：帝王切開時に偶発的な付属器腫瘤を認めた症例は119例で、発生頻度は1/329であった。最も多い組織診断は成熟嚢胞性奇形腫（32%）と機能性嚢胞（26%）であった。6例（5%）は両側性であった。腫瘤の平均径は6.4cmで、2例は悪性であった。結論：帝王切開時に偶発的に発見された腫瘤は、悪性の除外および帝王切開後の追加手術を避けるため、摘出すべきである。
